Trim Conserved Alignment Blocks with Gblocks

gblocks.Rd

User-facing wrapper for Gblocks that executes alignment trimming, renames Gblocks' default output file cleanly (e.g., _gb.fasta), and returns the output file path.

Usage

gblocks(
  input,
  output = NULL,
  t = "d",
  b1 = "min",
  b2 = "min",
  b3 = 20,
  b4 = 2,
  b5 = "a",
  args = NULL,
  exec = "Gblocks",
  browse = TRUE
)

Arguments

input

Character. Path to the input FASTA file.

output

Character or NULL. Custom path for the trimmed FASTA file. If NULL (default), inserts _gb before the file extension.

t

Character. Sequence type: "d" (DNA), "p" (Protein), or "c" (Codons). Default is "d".

b1

Numeric or "min". Minimum number of sequences for a conserved position. When "min", calculated as ceiling(n_seq / 2) + 1. Default is "min".

b2

Numeric or "min". Minimum number of sequences for a flank position. When "min", equals b1. Default is "min".

b3

Integer. Maximum number of contiguous non-conserved positions. Default is 20.

b4

Integer. Minimum block length. Default is 2.

b5

Character. Allowed gap positions: "a" (All), "h" (Half), or "n" (None). Default is "a".

args

Character vector or NULL. Additional CLI arguments passed to Gblocks. Default is NULL.

exec

Character. Path or command for the Gblocks executable. Default is "Gblocks".

browse

Logical. If TRUE, opens the generated HTML visualization in a browser. Default is TRUE.

Value

Character path to the trimmed FASTA alignment file.

See also

Other alignment: check_polish(), codon_summary(), concatenate_alignment(), mafft(), polish_alignment(), split_concat_alignment(), summarize_alignment(), test_sub_model(), trim_empty_columns()
